newsitem.title: USA: Reno to decide soon on outside fund-raising counsel.
newsitem.headline: Reno to decide soon on outside fund-raising counsel.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno will respond Monday to a congressional Republican request for an independent investigation into alleged Democratic campaign funding abuses, a Justice Department official said Thursday.
Although the official declined to say what her decision will be, Reno repeatedly has said an independent counsel was unwarranted, and there have been no signs of any change in her position so far.
Acting Deputy Attorney General Seth Waxman said the 30-day deadline set by the law for Reno to respond to the request from Republicans on the House and Senate judiciary committees falls on Saturday.
"Therefore, under law, the report is due on Monday. And we will respond on that day," Waxman said at the weekly Justice Department news briefing.

"I think it is in the best interests of everyone to let our response to Congress speak for itself. We are doing our very best, as appropriate, to make the most fulsome possible response to the inquiry made by the judiciary committees, and that will be available by Monday," he said.

Waxman emphasised that the independent counsel law requires "specific information" from a "credible source" that a covered official has committed a federal crime. Reno has held that this threshold has not been met.

In the event Reno changes her mind, she then would take the step sought by the congressional Republicans and open a preliminary inquiry lasting at least 90 days to determine whether to seek an independent counsel.

A Justice Department task force made up of career prosecutors and more than 30 FBI agents was investigating the fund-raising controversy that has dogged President Clinton, Vice President Al Gore and the Democratic Party.

"The attorney general is personally supervising that investigation, was personally supervising it before the requests from the judiciary committees came for the appointment of an independent counsel," Waxman said.
"She has entrusted the day-to-day management of the investigation" to career prosecutors who have served in both Democratic and Republican administrations, he said.
Reno has told the prosecutors to advise her if they come across any evidence that would trigger an independent counsel. "That is still the status of the investigation," Waxman said.

Judiciary Committee Democrats have told Reno that if it was determined that an independent counsel was warranted, the probe should include the "full scope of fund-raising irregularities" involving Republicans as well as Democrats.
The actual appointment of the independent counsel is made not by Reno, but by a special three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals.
